notes.heading: Keep concentration, dilution and reaction ratios distinct
paragraphs: Concentration describes an amount per volume, while a balanced equation relates reacting amounts. Before using a concentration expressed in moles per cubic decimetre, convert the volume to cubic decimetres. Dilution changes concentration by adding solvent without changing the amount of solute, provided none is lost or reacts. Mixing two reactants is different: first calculate their amounts, then compare the stoichiometric requirements. A unit check can expose a factor-of-one-thousand error even when the algebra appears correct.

questions.prompt: A solution has concentration 0.20 mol dm⁻³. Calculate the amount of solute in 75 cm³, showing the volume conversion.
25 cm³ of a 0.80 mol dm⁻³ solution is diluted to a final volume of 100 cm³ without reaction or solute loss. Find the final concentration and explain the conservation used.
questions.answer: 0.20 mol dm⁻³; the solute amount remains 0.020 mol.
markingPoints: State concentration and conservation of solute amount.

questions.prompt: In an idealised reaction H₂SO₄+2NaOH→Na₂SO₄+2H₂O, mix 0.030 mol acid with 0.040 mol NaOH. Find the limiting reactant and the acid remaining after complete reaction.
questions.answer: NaOH limits the reaction; 0.010 mol acid remains.
solution: The 0.040 mol NaOH consumes 0.040/2=0.020 mol acid.
Subtract the reacted acid from 0.030 mol.
